item.title: How to snapshot test Vue components
item.description: Snapshot tests capture the rendered output of components and alert you when it changes unexpectedly. As the creator of CoreUI, I’ve used snapshot testing to catch accidental regressions in UI components across hundreds of components. The standard approach uses @vue/test-utils to mount components and Vitest’s toMatchSnapshot to compare renders against stored snapshots. This provides an automatic safety net for your component’s output.

item.title: How to archive repository in Git
item.description:
Git archive creates compressed snapshots of repository contents without version control metadata, perfect for distribution packages and deployment artifacts. As the creator of CoreUI, I’ve used git archive to generate release packages for applications serving millions of users, creating clean distribution files without.git directories that reduce package size by 90%.

The most reliable approach uses git archive with compression for specific commits or branches.

item.title: How to snapshot test components in React
item.description: Snapshot testing in React captures component output and compares it against stored snapshots to catch unexpected UI changes. As the creator of CoreUI, I’ve used snapshot tests extensively to prevent UI regressions. Jest provides built-in snapshot testing that creates readable snapshots of React component trees and markup. This approach catches unintended changes in component structure, props, and rendered output without manual assertions.
